```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced in A. Several directly comparable competitors publish live prices: Foray at $60 per blueprint or $299/mo, MarketGeist at $49/mo Starter, and Insightloop at $99/mo. In B, every named direct competitor (Foundry, People.Build, Nixbly) is free and pre-revenue. B's only price anchor, CoFoundersLab at $29/mo, comes from an adjacent co-founder-matching category, is sourced through a third-party listicle, and carries a class-action billing complaint.",
    "A's concept is defined: reframe a decision, research the market, present trade-offs. B's brief says its own idea is unconfirmed ('one-line description to confirm') and that the customer 'varies by idea'. Committing a 90-day sprint to an undefined product and payer is a weaker first bet.",
    "A's saturation is among competitors that appear to be charging. B's saturation is among no-traction projects, some showing labelled dummy data or fake profiles. That pattern suggests weak demand or a commodity format, not proven demand.",
    "B's demand evidence contains a direct rebuttal of its premise from the same thread: 'you can just vibe code if you have an idea.' The brief also notes that AI coding tools are eroding the core need. A's two demand quotes describe the underlying pain without contradicting it in the same source.",
    "Both ideas can be built by a solo founder with agents. A's brief cites existing small-team agentic pipelines as proof. B's buildability rests only on competitors being thin landing pages. Buildability therefore does not separate them, and the payer evidence decides it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is a single vague post ('Looking for someone to make apps with lmk if your interested'), accessed through a Reddit mirror. It does not show anyone willing to pay, and the same thread contains a rebuttal of the premise. A close second is the $100-200 per paying customer acquisition estimate, which comes from a vendor blog that the brief itself says is not independently verified.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins mainly because B is weak, not because A is strong. A's case has serious unresolved problems. The niche is crowded with better-resourced competitors that run 250+ data sources. Paid acquisition (~$104 cost per lead) is out of line with a ~$60 one-off price. The category's own vendors admit a human must verify every number. A's demand quotes ('Only you can') arguably suggest people don't want a tool to make the decision for them. A still needs a differentiated wedge and an organic channel to reach a paying customer within 90 days. On the briefs alone, though, A has clearer payer evidence and a defined product."
}
```
